name: debezium-oracle
title: Debezium Oracle Connector
description: Capture changes from an Oracle database.
label: database

properties.name: name
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Unique name for the connector. Attempting to register again with the same name will fail.

properties.name: additionalProperties
properties.label: common
properties.description: Additional properties for debezium components in case they can't be set directly on the camel configurations (e.g: setting Kafka Connect properties needed by Debezium engine, for example setting KafkaOffsetBackingStore), the properties have to be prefixed with additionalProperties.. E.g: additionalProperties.transactional.id=12345&additionalProperties.schema.registry.url=http://localhost:8811/avro. This is a multi-value option with prefix: additionalProperties.

properties.name: internalKeyConverter
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The Converter class that should be used to serialize and deserialize key data for offsets. The default is JSON converter.

properties.name: internalValueConverter
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The Converter class that should be used to serialize and deserialize value data for offsets. The default is JSON converter.

properties.name: offsetCommitPolicy
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The name of the Java class of the commit policy. It defines when offsets commit has to be triggered based on the number of events processed and the time elapsed since the last commit. This class must implement the interface 'OffsetCommitPolicy'. The default is a periodic commit policy based upon time intervals.

properties.name: offsetCommitTimeoutMs
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Maximum number of milliseconds to wait for records to flush and partition offset data to be committed to offset storage before cancelling the process and restoring the offset data to be committed in a future attempt. The default is 5 seconds.

properties.name: offsetFlushIntervalMs
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Interval at which to try committing offsets. The default is 1 minute.

properties.name: offsetStorage
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The name of the Java class that is responsible for persistence of connector offsets.

properties.name: offsetStorageFileName
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Path to file where offsets are to be stored. Required when offset.storage is set to the FileOffsetBackingStore.

properties.name: offsetStoragePartitions
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The number of partitions used when creating the offset storage topic. Required when offset.storage is set to the 'KafkaOffsetBackingStore'.

properties.name: offsetStorageReplicationFactor
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Replication factor used when creating the offset storage topic. Required when offset.storage is set to the KafkaOffsetBackingStore

properties.name: offsetStorageTopic
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The name of the Kafka topic where offsets are to be stored. Required when offset.storage is set to the KafkaOffsetBackingStore.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: archiveDestinationName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Sets the specific archive log destination as the source for reading archive logs.When not set, the connector will automatically select the first LOCAL and VALID destination.

properties.name: archiveLogHours
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The number of hours in the past from SYSDATE to mine archive logs. Using 0 mines all available archive logs

properties.name: binaryHandlingMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify how binary (blob, binary, etc.) columns should be represented in change events, including: 'bytes' represents binary data as byte array (default); 'base64' represents binary data as base64-encoded string; 'base64-url-safe' represents binary data as base64-url-safe-encoded string; 'hex' represents binary data as hex-encoded (base16) string

properties.name: captureMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the capture mode used to capture streaming changes from Oracle'primary' (the default) captures changes from the primary, specified by database. configurations, 'physical_standby' captures changes from a read-only physical standby, specified by secondary. configurations.

properties.name: columnExcludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Regular expressions matching columns to exclude from change events

properties.name: columnIncludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Regular expressions matching columns to include in change events

properties.name: columnPropagateSourceType
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A comma-separated list of regular expressions matching fully-qualified names of columns that adds the columns original type and original length as parameters to the corresponding field schemas in the emitted change records.

properties.name: connectionValidationTimeoutMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum time in milliseconds to wait for connection validation to complete. Defaults to 60 seconds.

properties.name: converters
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Optional list of custom converters that would be used instead of default ones. The converters are defined using '.type' config option and configured using options '.'

properties.name: customMetricTags
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The custom metric tags will accept key-value pairs to customize the MBean object name which should be appended the end of regular name, each key would represent a tag for the MBean object name, and the corresponding value would be the value of that tag the key is. For example: k1=v1,k2=v2

properties.name: customSanitizePattern
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Regular expression identifying configuration keys whose values should be masked. When set, this custom pattern replaces Debeziums default password masking pattern.

properties.name: databaseConnectionAdapter
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The adapter to use when capturing changes from the database. Options include: 'LogMiner': (the default) to capture changes using native Oracle LogMiner with buffered transactions; 'LogMiner_Unbuffered': to capture changes using native Oracle LogMiner without buffering; 'XStream': to capture changes using Oracle XStreams; 'OLR': to capture changes using OpenLogReplicator

properties.name: databaseDbname
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the database from which the connector should capture changes

properties.name: databaseHostname
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Resolvable hostname or IP address of the database server.

properties.name: databaseOutServerName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Name of the XStream Outbound server to connect to.

properties.name: databasePassword
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Password of the database user to be used when connecting to the database.

properties.name: databasePdbName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Name of the pluggable database when working with a multi-tenant set-up. The CDB name must be given via database.dbname in this case.

properties.name: databasePort
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Port of the database server.

properties.name: databaseQueryTimeoutMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Time to wait for a query to execute, given in milliseconds. Defaults to 600 seconds (600,000 ms); zero means there is no limit.

properties.name: databaseUrl
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Complete JDBC URL as an alternative to specifying hostname, port and database provided as a way to support alternative connection scenarios.

properties.name: databaseUser
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Name of the database user to be used when connecting to the database.

properties.name: datatypePropagateSourceType
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A comma-separated list of regular expressions matching the database-specific data type names that adds the data type's original type and original length as parameters to the corresponding field schemas in the emitted change records.

properties.name: decimalHandlingMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify how DECIMAL and NUMERIC columns should be represented in change events, including: 'precise' (the default) uses java.math.BigDecimal to represent values, which are encoded in the change events using a binary representation and Kafka Connect's 'org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Decimal' type; 'string' uses string to represent values; 'double' represents values using Java's 'double', which may not offer the precision but will be far easier to use in consumers.

properties.name: errorsMaxRetries
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of retries on connection errors before failing (-1 = no limit, 0 = disabled, 0 = num of retries).

properties.name: eventProcessingFailureHandlingMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify how failures during processing of events (i.e. when encountering a corrupted event) should be handled, including: 'fail' (the default) an exception indicating the problematic event and its position is raised, causing the connector to be stopped; 'warn' the problematic event and its position will be logged and the event will be skipped; 'ignore' the problematic event will be skipped.

properties.name: executorShutdownTimeoutMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum time in milliseconds to wait for task executor to shut down.

properties.name: extendedHeadersEnabled
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Enable/Disable Debezium context headers that provides essential metadata for tracking and identifying the source of CDC events in downstream processing systems.

properties.name: guardrailCollectionsLimitAction
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify the action to take when a guardrail collections limit is exceeded: 'warn' (the default) logs a warning message and continues processing; 'fail' stops the connector with an error.

properties.name: guardrailCollectionsMax
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of collections or tables that can be captured by the connector. When this limit is exceeded, the action specified by 'guardrail.collections.limit.action' will be taken. Set to 0 to disable this guardrail.

properties.name: heartbeatActionQuery
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The query executed with every heartbeat.

properties.name: heartbeatIntervalMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Length of an interval in milli-seconds in in which the connector periodically sends heartbeat messages to a heartbeat topic. Use 0 to disable heartbeat messages. Disabled by default.

properties.name: heartbeatTopicsPrefix
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The prefix that is used to name heartbeat topics.Defaults to __debezium-heartbeat.

properties.name: includeSchemaChanges
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Whether the connector should publish changes in the database schema to a Kafka topic with the same name as the database server ID. Each schema change will be recorded using a key that contains the database name and whose value include logical description of the new schema and optionally the DDL statement(s). The default is 'true'. This is independent of how the connector internally records database schema history.

properties.name: includeSchemaComments
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Whether the connector parse table and column's comment to metadata object. Note: Enable this option will bring the implications on memory usage. The number and size of ColumnImpl objects is what largely impacts how much memory is consumed by the Debezium connectors, and adding a String to each of them can potentially be quite heavy. The default is 'false'.

properties.name: incrementalSnapshotWatermarkingStrategy
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify the strategy used for watermarking during an incremental snapshot: 'insert_insert' both open and close signal is written into signal data collection (default); 'insert_delete' only open signal is written on signal data collection, the close will delete the relative open signal;

properties.name: intervalHandlingMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify how INTERVAL columns should be represented in change events, including: 'string' represents values as an exact ISO formatted string; 'numeric' (default) represents values using the inexact conversion into microseconds

properties.name: legacyDecimalHandlingStrategy
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Uses the legacy decimal handling behavior before DBZ-7882

properties.name: legacySnapshotMaxThreads
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When enabled, uses the legacy table-per-thread parallel snapshot algorithm. When set to false (the default), tables are split into chunks and processed across all snapshot threads, allowing for higher concurrency for snapshots.

properties.name: lobEnabled
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When set to 'false', the default, LOB fields will not be captured nor emitted. When set to 'true', the connector will capture LOB fields and emit changes for those fields like any other column type.

properties.name: logMiningArchiveLogOnlyMode
properties.displayName: Log Mining Archive Log Only Mode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When set to 'false', the default, the connector will mine both archive log and redo logs to emit change events. When set to 'true', the connector will only mine archive logs. There are circumstances where its advantageous to only mine archive logs and accept latency in event emission due to frequent revolving redo logs.

properties.name: logMiningArchiveLogOnlyScnPollIntervalMs
properties.displayName: Log Mining Archive Log Only Scn Poll Interval Ms
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The interval in milliseconds to wait between polls checking to see if the SCN is in the archive logs.

properties.name: logMiningBufferDeferredTransactionRetentionMs
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Deferred Transaction Retention Ms
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Duration in milliseconds to retain deferred transaction metadata for transactions that never emit a DML event. By default, deferred transaction metadata is retained for 24 hours. This is independent of log.mining.transaction.retention.ms which governs cached transactions with events.

properties.name: logMiningBufferDeferredTransactionStart
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Deferred Transaction Start
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls whether transaction start events are deferred when using buffered LogMiner. When enabled, transaction start events are stored in a lightweight metadata map. Transactions are only promoted to the transaction cache when a DML event is observed. The mining window is not pinned by transactions, allowing a block-by-block sliding window.

properties.name: logMiningBufferDropOnStop
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Drop On Stop
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When set to true the underlying buffer cache is not retained when the connector is stopped. When set to false (the default), the buffer cache is retained across restarts.

properties.name: logMiningBufferEhcacheEventsConfig
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Ehcache Events Config
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the inner body the Ehcache tag for the events cache, but should not include the nor the attributes as these are managed by Debezium.

properties.name: logMiningBufferEhcacheGlobalConfig
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Ehcache Global Config
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies any Ehcache global configurations such as services or persistence. This cannot include nor tags as these are managed by Debezium.

properties.name: logMiningBufferEhcacheProcessedtransactionsConfig
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Ehcache Processedtransactions Config
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the inner body the Ehcache tag for the processed transaction cache, but should not include the nor the attributes as these are managed by Debezium.

properties.name: logMiningBufferEhcacheRollbacksConfig
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Ehcache Rollbacks Config
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the inner body the Ehcache tag for the rollbacks cache, but should not include the nor the attributes as these are managed by Debezium.

properties.name: logMiningBufferEhcacheSchemachangesConfig
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Ehcache Schemachanges Config
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the inner body the Ehcache tag for the schema changes cache, but should not include the nor the attributes as these are managed by Debezium.

properties.name: logMiningBufferEhcacheTransactionsConfig
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Ehcache Transactions Config
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the inner body the Ehcache tag for the transaction cache, but should not include the nor the attributes as these are managed by Debezium.

properties.name: logMiningBufferInfinispanCacheEvents
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Infinispan Cache Events
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the XML configuration for the Infinispan 'events' cache

properties.name: logMiningBufferInfinispanCacheGlobal
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Infinispan Cache Global
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the XML configuration for the Infinispan 'global' configuration

properties.name: logMiningBufferInfinispanCacheProcessedTransactions
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Infinispan Cache Processed Transactions
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the XML configuration for the Infinispan 'processed-transactions' cache

properties.name: logMiningBufferInfinispanCacheRollbacks
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Infinispan Cache Rollbacks
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the XML configuration for the Infinispan 'rollbacks' cache

properties.name: logMiningBufferInfinispanCacheSchemaChanges
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Infinispan Cache Schema Changes
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the XML configuration for the Infinispan 'schema-changes' cache

properties.name: logMiningBufferInfinispanCacheTransactions
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Infinispan Cache Transactions
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the XML configuration for the Infinispan 'transactions' cache

properties.name: logMiningBufferMemoryLegacyTransactionStart
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Memory Legacy Transaction Start
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls whether transaction start events are deferred when using buffered LogMiner. When enabled, transaction start events are stored in a lightweight metadata map. Transactions are only promoted to the transaction cache when a DML event is observed. The mining window is not pinned by transactions, allowing a block-by-block sliding window.

properties.name: logMiningBufferTrackClientId
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Track Client Id
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This controls whether the 'CLIENT_ID' column values are tracked. When set to true (the default), the 'CLIENT_ID' values are buffered and provided in events when available. When set to false, the 'CLIENT_ID' column is excluded from the LogMiner query and its values are not buffered, reducing both the memory footprint and query bandwidth.

properties.name: logMiningBufferTrackCommitTimestamp
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Track Commit Timestamp
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This controls whether the 'COMMIT_TIMESTAMP' column values are tracked. When set to true (the default), the 'COMMIT_TIMESTAMP' values are buffered and provided in events when available. When set to false, the 'COMMIT_TIMESTAMP' column is excluded from the LogMiner query and its values are not buffered, reducing both the memory footprint and query bandwidth.

properties.name: logMiningBufferTrackRsId
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Track Rs Id
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This controls whether the 'RS_ID' column values are tracked. When set to true (the default), the 'RS_ID' values are buffered and provided in events when available. When set to false, the 'RS_ID' column is excluded from the LogMiner query and its values are not buffered, reducing both the memory footprint and query bandwidth.

properties.name: logMiningBufferTrackStartTimestamp
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Track Start Timestamp
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This controls whether the 'START_TIMESTAMP' column values are tracked. When set to true (the default), the 'START_TIMESTAMP' values are buffered and provided in events when available. When set to false, the 'START_TIMESTAMP' column is excluded from the LogMiner query and its values are not buffered, reducing both the memory footprint and query bandwidth.

properties.name: logMiningBufferTrackUsername
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This controls whether the 'USERNAME' column values are tracked. When set to true (the default), the 'USERNAME' values are buffered and provided in events when available. When set to false, the 'USERNAME' column is excluded from the LogMiner query and its values are not buffered, reducing both the memory footprint and query bandwidth.

properties.name: logMiningBufferTransactionEventsThreshold
properties.displayName: Log Mining Buffer Transaction Events Threshold
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The number of events a transaction can include before the transaction is discarded. This is useful for managing buffer memory and/or space when dealing with very large transactions. Defaults to 0, meaning that no threshold is applied and transactions can have unlimited events.

properties.name: logMiningBufferType
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The buffer type controls how the connector manages buffering transaction data. memory - Uses the JVM process' heap to buffer all transaction data. infinispan_embedded - This option uses an embedded Infinispan cache to buffer transaction data and persist it to disk. infinispan_remote - This option uses a remote Infinispan cluster to buffer transaction data and persist it to disk. ehcache - Use ehcache in embedded mode to buffer transaction data and persist it to disk.

properties.name: logMiningClientidExcludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Comma separated list of client ids to exclude from LogMiner query.

properties.name: logMiningClientidIncludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Comma separated list of client ids to include from LogMiner query.

properties.name: logMiningFlushTableName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the flush table used by the connector, defaults to LOG_MINING_FLUSH.

properties.name: logMiningIncludeRedoSql
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When enabled, the transaction log REDO SQL will be included in the source information block.

properties.name: logMiningLogCountMin
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies the minimum number of logs to mine per redo thread. Setting this to 0 disables the cap, and all available logs are mined in a single pass.

properties.name: logMiningPathDictionary
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This is required when using the connector against a read-only database replica.

properties.name: logMiningQueryFilterMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specifies how the filter configuration is applied to the LogMiner database query. none - The query does not apply any schema or table filters, all filtering is at runtime by the connector. in - The query uses SQL in-clause expressions to specify the schema or table filters. regex - The query uses Oracle REGEXP_LIKE expressions to specify the schema or table filters.

properties.name: logMiningReadOnly
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When set to 'true', the connector will not attempt to flush the LGWR buffer to disk, allowing connecting to read-only databases.

properties.name: logMiningReadonlyHostname
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The secondary Oracle instance where changes will be streamed

properties.name: logMiningRestartConnection
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Debezium opens a database connection and keeps that connection open throughout the entire streaming phase. In some situations, this can lead to excessive SGA memory usage. By setting this option to 'true' (the default is 'false'), the connector will close and re-open a database connection after every detected log switch or if the log.mining.session.max.ms has been reached.

properties.name: logMiningSessionMaxMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that a LogMiner session lives for before being restarted. Defaults to 0 (indefinite until a log switch occurs)

properties.name: logMiningStrategy
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Defines the mining strategy and LogMiner session characteristics: 'redo_log_catalog' writes the data dictionary to the redo logs, is deprecated and will be removed in 3.7, 'online_catalog' uses the existing data dictionary and operates faster than 'redo_log_catalog' but requires schema changes in lock-step, 'hybrid' uses the existing data dictionary, operates faster than 'redo_log_catalog', and supports interleaved schema changes.

properties.name: logMiningTransactionRetentionMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Duration in milliseconds to keep long running transactions in transaction buffer between log mining sessions. By default, all transactions are retained.

properties.name: logMiningUsernameExcludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Comma separated list of usernames to exclude from LogMiner query.

properties.name: logMiningUsernameIncludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Comma separated list of usernames to include from LogMiner query.

properties.name: logMiningWindowMaxMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of milliseconds that the mining window can span. If a transaction remains open for longer than this duration, the mining window start SCN will be advanced to minimize the window size, preventing it from growing indefinitely. Defaults to 0 (disabled).

properties.name: maxBatchSize
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Maximum size of each batch of source records. Defaults to 2048.

properties.name: maxQueueSize
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Maximum size of the queue for change events read from the database log but not yet recorded or forwarded. Defaults to 8192, and should always be larger than the maximum batch size.

properties.name: maxQueueSizeInBytes
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Maximum size of the queue in bytes for change events read from the database log but not yet recorded or forwarded. Defaults to 0. Mean the feature is not enabled

properties.name: memoryManagementSchemasClass
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The fully-qualified class name of the storage implementation for schema metadata. The class must implement io.debezium.relational.TableMappingStorage. Defaults to io.debezium.relational.ConcurrentMapTableMappingStorage for in-memory storage.

properties.name: memoryManagementTablesClass
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The fully-qualified class name of the storage implementation for table metadata. The class must implement io.debezium.relational.TableMappingStorage. Defaults to io.debezium.relational.ConcurrentMapTableMappingStorage for in-memory storage.

properties.name: messageKeyColumns
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A semicolon-separated list of expressions that match fully-qualified tables and column(s) to be used as message key. Each expression must match the pattern ':', where the table names could be defined as (DB_NAME.TABLE_NAME) or (SCHEMA_NAME.TABLE_NAME), depending on the specific connector, and the key columns are a comma-separated list of columns representing the custom key. For any table without an explicit key configuration the table's primary key column(s) will be used as message key. Example: dbserver1.inventory.orderlines:orderId,orderLineId;dbserver1.inventory.orders:id

properties.name: notificationEnabledChannels
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: List of notification channels names that are enabled.

properties.name: notificationSinkTopicName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the topic for the notifications. This is required in case 'sink' is in the list of enabled channels

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationConfigFilePath
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Path to OpenLineage file configuration. See https://openlineage.io/docs/client/java/configuration

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationDatasetKafkaBootstrapServers
properties.displayName: Openlineage Integration Dataset Kafka Bootstrap Servers
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The Kafka bootstrap server address used as input/output namespace/

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationEnabled
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Enable Debezium to emit data lineage metadata through OpenLineage API

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationJobDescription
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The job's description emitted by Debezium

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationJobNamespace
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The job's namespace emitted by Debezium

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationJobOwners
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The job's owners emitted by Debezium. A comma-separated list of key-value pairs.For example: k1=v1,k2=v2

properties.name: openlineageIntegrationJobTags
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The job's tags emitted by Debezium. A comma-separated list of key-value pairs.For example: k1=v1,k2=v2

properties.name: openlogreplicatorHost
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The hostname of the OpenLogReplicator network service

properties.name: openlogreplicatorPort
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The port of the OpenLogReplicator network service

properties.name: openlogreplicatorSource
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The configured logical source name in the OpenLogReplicator configuration that is to stream changes

properties.name: pollIntervalMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Time to wait for new change events to appear after receiving no events, given in milliseconds. Defaults to 500 ms.

properties.name: postProcessors
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Optional list of post processors. The processors are defined using '.type' config option and configured using options ''

properties.name: provideTransactionMetadata
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Enables transaction metadata extraction together with event counting

properties.name: queryFetchSize
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of records that should be loaded into memory while streaming. A value of '0' uses the default JDBC fetch size, defaults to '2000'.

properties.name: racNodes
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A comma-separated list of RAC node hostnames or ip addresses

properties.name: retriableRestartConnectorWaitMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Time to wait before restarting connector after retriable exception occurs. Defaults to 10000ms.

properties.name: schemaHistoryInternal
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the SchemaHistory class that should be used to store and recover database schema changes. The configuration properties for the history are prefixed with the 'schema.history.internal.' string.

properties.name: schemaHistoryInternalFileFilename
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The path to the file that will be used to record the database schema history

properties.name: schemaHistoryInternalSkipUnparseableDdl
properties.displayName: Schema History Internal Skip Unparseable Ddl
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls the action Debezium will take when it meets a DDL statement in binlog, that it cannot parse.By default the connector will stop operating but by changing the setting it can ignore the statements which it cannot parse. If skipping is enabled then Debezium can miss metadata changes.

properties.name: schemaHistoryInternalStoreOnlyCapturedDatabasesDdl
properties.displayName: Schema History Internal Store Only Captured Databases Ddl
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls what DDL will Debezium store in database schema history. By default (false) Debezium will store all incoming DDL statements. If set to true, then only DDL that manipulates a table from captured schema/database will be stored.

properties.name: schemaHistoryInternalStoreOnlyCapturedTablesDdl
properties.displayName: Schema History Internal Store Only Captured Tables Ddl
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls what DDL will Debezium store in database schema history. By default (false) Debezium will store all incoming DDL statements. If set to true, then only DDL that manipulates a captured table will be stored.

properties.name: schemaNameAdjustmentMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify how schema names should be adjusted for compatibility with the message converter used by the connector, including: 'avro' replaces the characters that cannot be used in the Avro type name with underscore; 'avro_unicode' replaces the underscore or characters that cannot be used in the Avro type name with corresponding unicode like _uxxxx. Note: _ is an escape sequence like backslash in Java;'none' does not apply any adjustment (default)

properties.name: secondaryDbname
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The secondary Oracle instance database name, if different from primary

properties.name: secondaryHostname
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The secondary Oracle instance where changes will be streamed

properties.name: secondaryPort
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The secondary Oracle instance port where changes will be streamed

properties.name: secondaryUrl
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The secondary Oracle instance connection string URL where changes will be streamed

properties.name: signalDataCollection
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the data collection that is used to send signals/commands to Debezium. For multi-partition mode connectors, multiple signal data collections can be specified as a comma-separated list. Signaling is disabled when not set.

properties.name: signalEnabledChannels
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: List of channels names that are enabled. Source channel is enabled by default

properties.name: signalPollIntervalMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Interval for looking for new signals in registered channels, given in milliseconds. Defaults to 5 seconds.

properties.name: skippedOperations
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The comma-separated list of operations to skip during streaming, defined as: 'c' for inserts/create; 'u' for updates; 'd' for deletes, 't' for truncates, and 'none' to indicate nothing skipped. By default, only truncate operations will be skipped.

properties.name: snapshotDatabaseErrorsMaxRetries
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The number of attempts to retry database errors during snapshots before failing.

properties.name: snapshotDelayMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A delay period before a snapshot will begin, given in milliseconds. Defaults to 0 ms.

properties.name: snapshotFetchSize
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of records that should be loaded into memory while performing a snapshot.

properties.name: snapshotIncludeCollectionList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This setting must be set to specify a list of tables/collections whose snapshot must be taken on creating or restarting the connector.

properties.name: snapshotLockingMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls how the connector holds locks on tables while performing the schema snapshot. The default is 'shared', which means the connector will hold a table lock that prevents exclusive table access for just the initial portion of the snapshot while the database schemas and other metadata are being read. The remaining work in a snapshot involves selecting all rows from each table, and this is done using a flashback query that requires no locks. However, in some cases it may be desirable to avoid locks entirely which can be done by specifying 'none'. This mode is only safe to use if no schema changes are happening while the snapshot is taken.

properties.name: snapshotLockTimeoutMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of millis to wait for table locks at the beginning of a snapshot. If locks cannot be acquired in this time frame, the snapshot will be aborted. Defaults to 10 seconds

properties.name: snapshotMaxThreads
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The maximum number of threads used to perform the snapshot. Defaults to 1.

properties.name: snapshotMaxThreadsMultiplier
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The factor used to scale the number of snapshot chunks per table. The default behavior is to take 'row_count/snapshot.max.threads' to compute the number of rows per chunks. This may not be ideal for larger tables, and using the multiplier, the formula is adjusted to increase the number of chunks by using 'row_count/(snapshot.max.threads snapshot.max.threads.multiplier).

properties.name: snapshotMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The criteria for running a snapshot upon startup of the connector. Select one of the following snapshot options: 'always': The connector runs a snapshot every time that it starts. After the snapshot completes, the connector begins to stream changes from the redo logs.; 'initial' (default): If the connector does not detect any offsets for the logical server name, it runs a snapshot that captures the current full state of the configured tables. After the snapshot completes, the connector begins to stream changes from the redo logs. 'initial_only': The connector performs a snapshot as it does for the 'initial' option, but after the connector completes the snapshot, it stops, and does not stream changes from the redo logs.; 'schema_only': If the connector does not detect any offsets for the logical server name, it runs a snapshot that captures only the schema (table structures), but not any table data. After the snapshot completes, the connector begins to stream changes from the redo logs.; 'schema_only_recovery': The connector performs a snapshot that captures only the database schema history. The connector then transitions to streaming from the redo logs. Use this setting to restore a corrupted or lost database schema history topic. Do not use if the database schema was modified after the connector stopped.

properties.name: snapshotModeConfigurationBasedSnapshotData
properties.displayName: Snapshot Mode Configuration Based Snapshot Data
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When 'snapshot.mode' is set as configuration_based, this setting permits to specify whenever the data should be snapshotted or not.

properties.name: snapshotModeConfigurationBasedSnapshotOnDataError
properties.displayName: Snapshot Mode Configuration Based Snapshot On Data Error
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When 'snapshot.mode' is set as configuration_based, this setting permits to specify whenever the data should be snapshotted or not in case of error.

properties.name: snapshotModeConfigurationBasedSnapshotOnSchemaError
properties.displayName: Snapshot Mode Configuration Based Snapshot On Schema Error
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When 'snapshot.mode' is set as configuration_based, this setting permits to specify whenever the schema should be snapshotted or not in case of error.

properties.name: snapshotModeConfigurationBasedSnapshotSchema
properties.displayName: Snapshot Mode Configuration Based Snapshot Schema
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When 'snapshot.mode' is set as configuration_based, this setting permits to specify whenever the schema should be snapshotted or not.

properties.name: snapshotModeConfigurationBasedStartStream
properties.displayName: Snapshot Mode Configuration Based Start Stream
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When 'snapshot.mode' is set as configuration_based, this setting permits to specify whenever the stream should start or not after snapshot.

properties.name: snapshotModeCustomName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: When 'snapshot.mode' is set as custom, this setting must be set to specify a the name of the custom implementation provided in the 'name()' method. The implementations must implement the 'Snapshotter' interface and is called on each app boot to determine whether to do a snapshot.

properties.name: snapshotSelectStatementOverrides
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: This property contains a comma-separated list of fully-qualified tables (DB_NAME.TABLE_NAME) or (SCHEMA_NAME.TABLE_NAME), depending on the specific connectors. Select statements for the individual tables are specified in further configuration properties, one for each table, identified by the id 'snapshot.select.statement.overrides.DB_NAME.TABLE_NAME' or 'snapshot.select.statement.overrides.SCHEMA_NAME.TABLE_NAME', respectively. The value of those properties is the select statement to use when retrieving data from the specific table during snapshotting. A possible use case for large append-only tables is setting a specific point where to start (resume) snapshotting, in case a previous snapshotting was interrupted.

properties.name: snapshotTablesOrderByRowCount
properties.displayName: Snapshot Tables Order By Row Count
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Controls the order in which tables are processed in the initial snapshot. A descending value will order the tables by row count descending. A ascending value will order the tables by row count ascending. A value of disabled (the default) will disable ordering by row count.

properties.name: sourceinfoStructMaker
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the SourceInfoStructMaker class that returns SourceInfo schema and struct.

properties.name: statisticsMetricsEnabled
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Enable to collect various kind of statistics, like latencies in record processing, and derived data like quantiles. By default collecting statistics is enabled.

properties.name: streamingDelayMs
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A delay period after the snapshot is completed and the streaming begins, given in milliseconds. Defaults to 0 ms.

properties.name: tableExcludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: A comma-separated list of regular expressions that match the fully-qualified names of tables to be excluded from monitoring

properties.name: tableIncludeList
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The tables for which changes are to be captured

properties.name: timePrecisionMode
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Time, date, and timestamps can be represented with different kinds of precisions, including: 'adaptive' (the default) bases the precision of time, date, and timestamp values on the database column's precision; 'adaptive_time_microseconds' like 'adaptive' mode, but TIME fields always use microseconds precision; 'connect' always represents time, date, and timestamp values using Kafka Connect's built-in representations for Time, Date, and Timestamp, which uses millisecond precision regardless of the database columns' precision; 'isostring' represents time, date, and timestamp values as ISO-8601 formatted strings at the UTC time zone; 'microseconds' always represents time, date, and timestamp values using microsecond precision; 'nanoseconds' always represents time, date, and timestamp values using nanosecond precision.

properties.name: tombstonesOnDelete
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Whether delete operations should be represented by a delete event and a subsequent tombstone event (true) or only by a delete event (false). Emitting the tombstone event (the default behavior) allows Kafka to completely delete all events pertaining to the given key once the source record got deleted.

properties.name: topicNamingStrategy
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: The name of the TopicNamingStrategy class that should be used to determine the topic name for data change, schema change, transaction, heartbeat event etc.

properties.name: topicPrefix
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Topic prefix that identifies and provides a namespace for the particular database server/cluster is capturing changes. The topic prefix should be unique across all other connectors, since it is used as a prefix for all Kafka topic names that receive events emitted by this connector. Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, dots and underscores must be accepted.

properties.name: transactionMetadataFactory
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Class to make transaction context & transaction struct/schemas

properties.name: unavailableValuePlaceholder
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Specify the constant that will be provided by Debezium to indicate that the original value is unavailable and not provided by the database.

properties.name: xstreamOutServerName
properties.label: consumer,oracle
properties.description: Name of the XStream Outbound server to connect to.
